Individual Assignment: Problem Discovery and Solution Proposal
Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this individual assignment is to identify a real-world problem that could be addressed through an end-to-end software solution. You will investigate the problem, understand how it is addressed today, identify gaps in existing approaches, and propose a solution that could realistically be developed by a team during the semester. Your proposal may focus on either industry impact or social impact.
Selected ideas from the individual assignments may become the basis for semester team projects. Therefore, choose a problem that is important enough to matter but sufficiently scoped for a team of 4–6 students to prototype within one semester.
By the end of the semester, the team must deliver a functioning end-to-end solution, not merely a proposal, presentation, UI mockup, or isolated algorithm.
Must Have: Capabilities necessary to demonstrate the core value proposition.
Be deliberate about scope. A smaller system that works end-to-end is preferable to an ambitious system that remains incomplete.
1. Problem and Current Landscape
Define the problem you want to address.
Problem Definition
Clearly describe:
What is the problem?
Who experiences the problem?
In what context does it occur?
Why is it important to solve?
Prevalence and Significance
Provide evidence that the problem is meaningful and sufficiently prevalent.
Depending on your topic, relevant evidence might include:
Number or percentage of people or organizations affected
Size of the relevant industry or market
Financial costs
Time or productivity losses
Social consequences
Current trends indicating that the problem is growing or changing
Support important claims with credible sources.
Target Users and Stakeholders
Identify the primary target users of your proposed solution.
Also consider other stakeholders who may influence adoption or be affected by the solution. These may include customers, employers, administrators, regulators, healthcare providers, educators, community organizations, or other groups.
Distinguish, where appropriate, among:
User: Who interacts with the solution?
Customer: Who pays for or purchases it?
Beneficiary: Who ultimately receives the value?
These may or may not be the same person.
How the Problem Is Addressed Today
Investigate the current landscape.
Describe how people or organizations currently solve or manage the problem. Consider:
Existing software products
Commercial competitors
Manual workflows
Institutional processes
Open-source solutions
Workarounds
Cases in which users simply tolerate the problem
Identify at least 2–3 existing approaches or alternatives.
2. Proposed Solution
Propose an end-to-end software solution that addresses the unmet need identified above.
Your proposal should explain:
What the solution does
Who will use it
What information or inputs it requires
What processing, software, or intelligence occurs
What output or action it produces
How the user receives value
Why someone would choose it over the current alternatives
Describe the proposed workflow from beginning to end.
Value Proposition
Complete this sentence: For [target user], who struggles with [problem], our proposed solution provides [key benefit] by [how it works], unlike [current alternative(s)], which [important limitation].
Measuring Impact
Define how you would determine whether the project succeeds.
Identify 3-5 measurable success criteria. Examples include:
Reduction in task completion time
Improvement in accuracy
Reduction in cost
Increase in user engagement
User satisfaction
Reduction in errors
System reliability
Adoption or retention
Accessibility improvements
Measurable social outcomes
At least one metric should evaluate technical performance, and at least one should evaluate user, business, or social impact.
Deliverable
Submit a 2 page proposal, excluding references and optional appendices.
Problem significance (20%)
Is the problem real, important, and supported by evidence?
Understanding of users and current solutions (20%)
Does the proposal demonstrate a strong understanding of stakeholders, existing approaches, and the unmet need?
Solution quality and differentiation (20%)
Does the proposed solution logically address the identified problem, and is its value proposition compelling?
Feasibility and scope (20%)
Could a team of 4–6 graduate students realistically implement an end-to-end MVP during the semester?
Impact and measurability (10%)
Are the expected industry or social benefits meaningful and measurable?
Clarity and professionalism (10%)
Is the proposal well researched, logically organized, concise, and professionally presented?
Important Principle
Do not optimize your proposal for technological novelty alone.
Meaningful Problem × User Need × Technical Feasibility × Effective Execution × Measurable Impact

items.back: It is an AI-powered system designed to help solar-powered households optimize their energy consumption and renewable energy utilization through personalized recommendations and forecasts.

Project Title
AI Home Energy Copilot for Solar-Powered Households Using Multi-Agent Forecasting
Project Abstract
Issue Statement
Residential solar adoption continues to grow, yet many homeowners struggle to understand
and optimize their energy usage. Even homes equipped with solar panels often rely on static
dashboards that show historical consumption and generation data but provide little guidance
about future energy availability, battery utilization, grid dependence, or cost-saving
opportunities. As electricity prices rise and grids become increasingly stressed, helping
households make intelligent energy decisions can reduce costs, improve renewable energy
utilization, and contribute to broader sustainability goals. The challenge impacts millions of
households transitioning toward clean energy systems.
Existing Solutions
Current platforms from solar providers and utility companies primarily focus on monitoring past
energy consumption and solar generation. Some systems provide simple forecasts based on
weather data, but they rarely offer personalized recommendations or account for household
behavior patterns, appliance usage, battery storage, dynamic electricity pricing, and grid
conditions simultaneously. Most solutions operate as standalone forecasting tools rather than
intelligent decision-support systems.
My Aim
This project proposes an AI-powered Home Energy Copilot that combines large language
models, multi-agent systems, and time-series forecasting models to help homeowners optimize
energy consumption and renewable energy utilization. Specialized agents would collaboratively
predict solar generation, forecast household demand, estimate electricity costs, monitor
battery health, and recommend energy-efficient actions. Responsible AI principles would be
incorporated through explainable recommendations, transparent uncertainty estimates,
privacy-preserving data handling, and fairness across different household types.
Examples of recommendations include:
• Best times to run energy-intensive appliances
• When to charge or discharge home batteries
• Anticipated grid electricity usage
• Potential monthly cost savings
• Carbon footprint reduction opportunities

ReAct:
Introduced in the 2022 paper “ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models” (Yao et al., arXiv:2210.03629 ), ReAct teaches LLMs to:
- Reason — break down problems into intermediate steps.
- Act — use tools (like search engines, APIs, calculators) to get more information.
- Reflect — revise and improve based on the outcome.
This happens in a loop, where each step includes both:
- a Thought (reasoning step),
- and an Action (tool use or lookup).

• Potential monthly cost savings
